Question: Who was the first musician to write a book?
Answer: David, the young shepherd who slew Goliath, was a harpist. Later he was anointed King of Israel and Judah. He wrote the Book of Psalms. One half of the Psalms are headed “A Psalm of David.” That all happened around 1000 BC. Much later Leonard Cohen mentioned David in “Hallelujah” as the man who played the “secret chord” that pleased the Lord. Cohen wrote several books BEFORE he became a musician, most notably the fine novel “Beautiful Losers.”

Question: Did the Beatles ever play Long and Winding Road live in concert?
Answer: No. McCartney wrote the song in 1968 and the Beatles recorded it on Jan. 26, 1969. The Beatles did perform the “Rooftop Concert” on Jan. 30, 1969, but the song wasn’t played that day. Otherwise, the Beatles had ended their concertizing career as a band with the performance on Aug. 26, 1966, at Candlestick Park in San Francisco, California.

Question: Who is the singer with The Beatles on Hey Bulldog?
Answer: The only singers on “Hey Bulldog” are John Lennon, who sang lead and Paul McCartney, who sang harmony. Both had fun making barking sounds. The song was recorded in a single ten-hour session on Feb. 11, 1968. A camera crew was there to shoot a promo film for “Lady Madonna,” but the Beatles decided to record another song, written primarily by Lennon, while they were there together in the studio. The resulting video is one of the last documents of the band playing with abandon and the sheer joy of making music together. The session was produced by George Martin and Geoff Emerick. Because “Hey Bulldog” only appeared on the “Yellow Submarine” soundtrack album, the song was relatively obscure for many years. However, in the past decade or so, it has become regarded as one of the Beatles’ best rockers. Ringo played drums, John played the piano, Paul played a wonderfully busy bass line and George played lead guitar, although George lent John his Gibson SG and John played the lead solo that was used on the recording.
